description:
FOUND s492 (Fable, 2026-09-20) by the everyday-Perl battery (#1994) -- a probe helper happened to be called `pass`.  PRE-EXISTING on main 268d7e00 (and at v0.1.0 by construction).

REPRODUCERS (probed vs perl 5.40.3; ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s492/probes/tapname2.pl, tapname4.pl, tapname.pl, chain1.pl):
  package A; sub note { "A-note" } sub skip { "A-skip" } sub helper { "A-helper" }
  package B; sub note { "B-note" } sub skip { "B-skip" } sub helper { "B-helper" }
  package main; print A::note(), " ", B::note(), " ", A::skip(), " ", B::skip(), " ", A::helper(), " ", B::helper();
      perl: A-note B-note A-skip B-skip A-helper B-helper        PCL: B-note B-note B-skip B-skip A-helper B-helper      <-- SILENT
  package Proj; sub new { bless {}, shift } sub plan { "p" }   package main; Proj->new->plan
      perl: p        PCL: DIES  Can't locate object method "plan" via package "Proj"
  sub pass { "mine" }  main->can("pass") ? "can" : "cannot"      perl: can      PCL: cannot   (calling pass() directly works; defined &pass / exists &main::pass are right)
No program here says `use Test::More`.  Ordinary names: a job queue's `->skip`, a document's `->note`, a planner's `->plan`, a validator's `->ok` / `->is`, `->fail`, `->pass`, `->like`, `->explain` ...

THE MECHANISM (measured, cl/pcl-runtime.lisp ~lines 150-159): the pcl package EXPORTS 25 `pl-NAME` symbols for the TAP layer (`#:pl-plan #:pl-done_testing #:pl-ok #:pl-is ... #:pl-explain #:pl-locales_enabled #:pl-_diag`; the only other exported `pl-` symbol is `pl-__SUB__`), and every perl package's CL package does `(:use :pcl)`.  So inside `package Proj` the emission `(p-sub pl-plan ...)` names the INHERITED symbol `pcl:pl-plan`: it REDEFINES the harness function for the whole image instead of defining `Proj::pl-plan`, a second package's definition overwrites the first, and method resolution / `can`, which look for a `pl-plan` whose home is the class's package, find nothing.  The export list's own comment says why it exists ("READ before the test lib loads -- without the eager export that interns a distinct main::pl-diag and the test lib's own (export ...) then dies with NAME-CONFLICT").

FIX SHAPE (design, Fable): the TAP functions must reach a package the way perl gives them to it -- by IMPORT, not by inheritance.  They keep living in ONE home package that user packages do NOT `:use` (cl/pcl-test.lisp's own package, or a `|Test::More|`-style one), exported from THERE, and `use Test::More` / `use Test::Simple` / perl-tests' `require "./test.pl"` (and whatever else the harness recognises today -- grep how `pl-ok` becomes callable in a .t file: it is by this inheritance alone, so EVERY test entry point must be enumerated first) install them into the USING package through the runtime's ordinary import path (the same fdefinition/glob aliasing `%p-do-import` performs for a shim).  A package that never imported them is then untouched; a package that imported them AND defines `sub note` redefines its OWN alias only, as perl does (with perl's "Subroutine note redefined" being a warning PCL need not print).  `pl-__SUB__` is not a TAP name -- measure whether a user `sub __SUB__` is even legal and leave it unless it shows the same bug.
WHAT NOT TO DO: no rename of the user's sub at emission time keyed on the 25 names (a name list in Pl/ -- 9a's smell test, and it breaks `Proj->can("plan")`, symbolic calls, `*Proj::plan{CODE}`, `defined &Proj::plan`); no shadowing-import of the 25 symbols in every defpackage (a per-package cost on every program for a test-only feature, and it breaks the .t files that rely on inheritance today).

THIS TOUCHES THE HARNESS, so both populations reach it: WHAT-TO-RUN-WHEN's harness row applies -- full sweep (TOTAL must equal the baseline exactly: every .t file calls these functions) AND the companion `--all --quick`, baselines edited ROW BY ROW; `tools/ir-inventory.pl` regenerated (exports move; `Pl/t/ir-inventory-01.t`); `tools/ir-host-leak.pl`; the CPAN board (its .t files use Test::More through the same door) by ROWS; the Pl/t gate's `run_cl`/`test_transpile` helpers call the TAP layer too -- the gate is the first bar.  A saved CORE must be rebuilt by the change itself (content-keyed, automatic).  Guard: the three reproducers above in a new Pl/t file, INVERSE-verified, plus a row that a .t-style program `use Test::More tests => 1; sub note { "mine" } ok(note() eq "mine")` behaves as perl.
SIZE: a harness/load-model change, NOT a filler -- its own batch member with a stop rule; if the import route cannot be made to work inside one agent-day, the fallback to MEASURE (not ship blind) is `shadow` of the 25 names at defpackage time for packages that are not TAP users.


=== DOOR TABLE + BLOCKERS (s492b, 2026-09-21 â NOT SHIPPED) ===
The task's mandated first step, done; the fix itself was NOT attempted (see WHY below).

EVERY DOOR THROUGH WHICH A PROGRAM GETS ok/is/plan/... TODAY (grepped, not guessed):
  D1  `use Test::More` / `use Test::Simple` / `use Test2::Bundle::More`
      -> `p-use` sees the name in `*p-pcl-provided-modules*` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp ~22868),
         calls `p-ensure-test-lib` (~22891) which LOADS cl/pcl-test.lisp INTO :pcl, then
         `%TEST-IMPORT` for the plan arguments.  No symbol import happens at all: the names
         are reachable because :pcl EXPORTS them and every user package (:use :pcl)s.
         Population: 1 file in perl-tests/, most of the CPAN board's t/.
  D2  `require "./test.pl"` / `require "t/test.pl"` -- 102 of the 108 perl-tests files.
      THIS DOOR DOES NOT USE THE TAP LAYER AT ALL: perl-tests/t/test.pl is transpiled like
      user code and DEFINES `sub ok ($@)` at its line 882, `sub is ($$@)` at 883, ...
      Because :pcl exports pl-ok, those definitions land on `pcl::pl-ok` and REDEFINE the
      TAP layer's function for the whole image.  That is #2003's mechanism in its most
      consequential form, and it is also what makes the sweep work today.
  D3  the sweep runner: tools/sweep-perl-tests.pl loads cl/pcl-test.lisp explicitly
      (lines 107 and 199) before the program, and again for the skip registry.
  D4  the companion runner: tools/run-perl-suite.pl line 201, same shape; its saved core
      has the TAP layer COMPILED IN (its line 119 says so).
  D5  tools/run-dist-t.pl (the CPAN board) relies on D1.
  D6  lib/Test/More.pm is PROTOTYPE-ONLY -- never loaded at run time; it exists so
      `_extract_module_prototypes` can read the ($$;$) slots that #2004's context arm
      consumes.  A move must keep those prototypes readable.
  D7  Pl/t's own helpers do NOT call the TAP layer (PCLCore.pm has no pl-ok reference);
      the gate's .t files are PERL Test::More, run by prove, not by PCL.  One less door
      than the task assumed.
  D8  cl/skip-registry.lisp is loaded beside the TAP layer and keys on DESCRIPTIONS.
  D9  tools/ir-inventory.pl reads the TAP names from cl/pcl-test.lisp (line 517) and from
      the :pcl export list; moving them moves docs/ir-op-inventory.* and its gate row.

WHY IT WAS NOT SHIPPED HERE (and what the next attempt must answer FIRST):
  (a) THE EXPORT LIST'S OWN COMMENT IS THE BLOCKER (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp ~146): v2 hoists
      definition-bucket forms ABOVE the runtime `use Test::More` form, so a `pl-diag`
      reference is READ before the test lib loads.  Without the eager export the reader
      interns a distinct `main::pl-diag` and the lib's own `(export ...)` dies with
      SB-EXT:NAME-CONFLICT.  An IMPORT route must therefore install by
      `(setf (fdefinition (intern "PL-OK" caller-pkg)) ...)` into the ALREADY-INTERNED
      caller symbol and never re-export into :pcl -- that is believed to work, and it is
      the first thing to prove with a two-file probe.
  (b) REMOVING THE INHERITANCE IS A BEHAVIOUR CHANGE FOR D2, AND IN PERL'S DIRECTION:
      after `require "./test.pl"` perl puts `ok` in MAIN only, so `package Foo; ok(1)`
      DIES in perl and WORKS in PCL today.  Rows that rely on PCL's extra permissiveness
      will start failing honestly -- they must be found (a gate-SET scan over both
      populations) and each one explained before the flip, not after.
  (c) The bar is the whole harness: full gate + full sweep with TOTAL == baseline exactly
      + companion --all --quick + the CPAN board by rows + ir-inventory regenerated.
      That is a session of its own; s492b spent its budget on the seven other members and
      would have had to rush this one's bar.  Shipping it on a rushed bar is the one
      outcome worse than not shipping it.

SIBLING #2100 IS DONE (s492b) and did NOT share a predicate with this one -- measured:
#2100 is `cl_name`'s plain-call arm reading `%RUNTIME_NAMES`, a COMPILER table; #2003 is
the :pcl package's export list, a RUNTIME/load-model fact.  Two mechanisms, two fixes.
subject: SILENT WRONG (everyday, pre-existing): a user sub or METHOD named like a TAP-harness function -- plan note skip ok is isnt like unlike pass fail diag explain cmp_ok is_deeply done_testing ... (25 names) -- is ONE SHARED FUNCTION across all packages: `package A; sub note {"A"} package B; sub note {"B"}` makes `A::note()` answer "B"; `$obj->plan` / `$obj->skip` DIE "Can't locate object method"; `main->can("ok")` is false
